news.title: OpenAI lets businesses claim their ChatGPT profile
news.description: OpenAI is testing a Businesses feature that lets companies manage their profile in ChatGPT, update their information and track interactions. Business Hub also allows them to add product catalogs and view mentions, views and clicks.

news.title: Google makes Gemini 4 Carbon available to the general public
news.description: After two weeks of limited availability to cybersecurity advocates, Gemini 4 Carbon is now accessible through Gemini, Search’s AI mode, Antigravity, or the API reserved for AI Ultra subscribers. Google says the model is particularly capable at complex, long-running tasks, precision knowledge, and data analysis.

news.title: SpaceX launches Starlink Mini 2 with removable battery and Wi-Fi 6
news.description: SpaceX has launched Starlink Mini 2, featuring a removable battery and Wi-Fi 6.

news.title: Claris tests Harbor, a local AI app for Macs
news.description: Claris, an Apple subsidiary, is testing Harbor, an app designed to run AI locally on Macs.

news.title: Ring unveils a flying drone and a robot to monitor homes
news.description: The Ring Drone Cam is a $250 flying security camera, while the Ring Rover Cam costs $1,000. They are scheduled to go on sale in the United States in December and January, subject to FCC approval for the drone.

news.title: Anthropic targets a $1.4 trillion valuation for its IPO
news.description: According to a regulatory filing, Anthropic could raise $90 billion and reach a $1.4 trillion valuation in its IPO. The company plans to offer its shares at between $70 and $78 and has already secured purchase commitments worth $26 billion.

news.title: OpenAI reportedly acquired travel startup Odessia
news.description: OpenAI reportedly acquired Odessia, a startup specializing in travel agents, but the company has not confirmed the deal.

news.title: OpenAI losses soar despite sharp revenue growth
news.description: OpenAI generated 10 billion dollars in revenue in the third quarter, but its operating loss reached 10.9 billion dollars. Revenue rose 50% from the previous quarter and tripled year over year.

news.title: Google Fi launches a “super network” that automatically chooses the carrier
news.description: Google Fi is launching a feature that lets phones automatically switch between two carriers to find the best signal. It is rolling out on Pixel 9 and later models with an eSIM, in more than 200 destinations.

news.title: TSMC invests up to one billion dollars in Anthropic and OpenAI
news.description: TSMC plans to acquire stakes in Anthropic and OpenAI worth up to one billion dollars.

news.title: IBM ends visa and green card sponsorship for most consultants
news.description: IBM is ending visa and green card sponsorship for most consulting positions.

news.title: AI agents discover an unmapped Maya site
news.description: AI agents have discovered a Maya site that was not on any maps.

news.title: Nvidia H200 AI chips reach blacklisted Chinese university
news.description: Nvidia H200 artificial intelligence chips have made their way to a Chinese university placed on a blacklist.

news.title: A Model Y owner looks back on another summer season
news.description: The title presents a review of another summer season with a Tesla Model Y.

news.title: Road noise and seals on the Tesla Model 3
news.description: The title presents a discussion about road noise and the seals on the Tesla Model 3.

news.title: Anthropic launches Claude Whiteboards, Sheets, and Data
news.description: Anthropic is rolling out three productivity tools: Whiteboards for creating visual boards, Sheets for designing shareable spreadsheets, and Data for turning metrics into narrated stories. They are available on paid plans in Claude’s Artifacts section.

news.title: ChatGPT Enterprise arrives on AWS Marketplace
news.description: OpenAI now offers ChatGPT Enterprise through AWS Marketplace, with purchasing, management, and billing handled through existing AWS accounts. Customers can use their AWS commitments and access specialized offerings for healthcare and finance.

news.title: Anthropic and OpenAI seek greater control over software development
news.description: Anthropic and OpenAI are expanding their features to handle more of the end-to-end software development process. The shift aims to increase the profitability and commercial value of their models.

news.title: An analysis predicts an artificial intelligence explosion in 2027
news.description: The arrival of a superhuman AI researcher is expected at some point in 2027, provided there is no major slowdown in development. AI systems capable of automating all office work could appear before 2028, while companies may not be ready to ensure their alignment.

news.title: Anthropic targets a $1.3 trillion stock-market valuation
news.description: Anthropic plans to sell 825 million shares at between $70 and $78 in an IPO expected next week. The company hopes to raise an additional $26 billion from major investors, including Google and AMD.

news.title: DeepMind verifies security properties of Signal’s code
news.description: Google DeepMind used AI agents and mathematically verified Lean theorems to prove security properties of Signal’s production code.

news.title: OpenAI studies AI’s effect on freelance work
news.description: OpenAI published a study on AI’s impact on independent workers. Detailed results were not yet available at the time of writing.

news.title: IGF jurors boycott AI after Big Walk studio’s admission
news.description: Independent Games Festival jurors refuse to vote for games that used generative AI. The studio behind Big Walk later acknowledged using AI sparingly to fix bugs late in development.

news.title: Disney+ offers more than 60 3D movies on Meta Quest headsets
news.description: The Disney+ app on Meta Quest adds more than 60 3D movies, including Toy Story 5, Avatar: Fire and Ash and The Avengers. The films can be watched in virtual settings such as Tatooine or Avengers Tower.

news.title: Eight countries and four AI companies pledge an emergency shutdown button
news.description: Eight countries, OpenAI, Anthropic, Microsoft and Mistral AI signed the Paris Call for AI Safety and Security. The text calls for shutdown mechanisms, independent audits and greater transparency, without sanctions or a timeline.

news.title: Anthropic’s seven co-founders could cash out $250 million each
news.description: According to the S-1 filing, each co-founder will sell 3,378,378 shares as part of the proposed IPO. The deal could value Anthropic at up to $1.4 trillion, while the founders would retain 51.1% of voting rights.

news.title: Building your first AI automation
news.description: Chapter 28 explains how to choose a low-risk first automation, describe it with a trigger, an action and an outcome, then build and test an automatic morning briefing. Set aside 15 minutes and have the assistant connected to the previous chapter.

news.title: Five questions to identify tasks to automate
news.description: Chapter 29 proposes identifying recurring tasks from a week of notes, then evaluating them with five questions, two of which can immediately eliminate a candidate. It also explains how to estimate the build cost and test the automation on a week that was already completed manually.

news.title: Claude takes on Microsoft Office with new workplace tools
news.description: Anthropic is launching new Claude tools for office work, including Meetings, Whiteboards, Sheets and Data. Claude Meetings can join video conferences and perform actions such as creating a timeline or searching for figures.

news.title: Apple to permanently shut down its support community
news.description: Apple will close its official Support Community forum, which will become read-only before permanently shutting down on November 20. The company is directing users to its official support website.

news.title: Grok Build vulnerability exposes thousands of users’ secrets
news.description: Grok Build, SpaceXSI’s coding agent, exposed data from thousands of users through shareable application links. The data included commercial projects, medical results and internal information.

news.title: Anthropic says AI is narrowing Nvidia’s CUDA lead
news.description: Anthropic says AI is eroding Nvidia’s lead in CUDA and has reduced the process of switching chips to AMD from several months to three days.

news.title: Regulator says evaluating academic work is nearly impossible with AI
news.description: A regulator says AI has made evaluating academic work “almost impossible.”

news.title: Railway vulnerability leads to 740,000 dollars in AI-related charges
news.description: An intrusion targeting Railway resulted in 740,000 dollars in fraudulent charges for AI services.

news.title: Europe wants to ban deceptive interfaces and loot boxes for minors
news.description: Europe wants to ban “dark patterns” in apps as well as loot boxes aimed at minors.

news.title: Kalshi warned of possible prosecution as authorities target prediction markets
news.description: Kalshi was reportedly warned of possible prosecution as federal authorities intensify their actions against prediction markets.

news.title: ByteDance reportedly preparing a Muse-inspired AI agent for the coming weeks
news.description: ByteDance is reportedly planning to launch an AI agent comparable to Muse in the coming weeks.

news.title: Microsoft finds AI agents can be hacked by modifying their network
news.description: Microsoft discovered that AI agents could be compromised by modifying fewer than ten neurons.

news.title: AMD launches EPYC Zen 6 processors for AI agent deployments
news.description: AMD has launched its EPYC Zen 6 chips, designed to enable denser deployments of AI agents.

news.title: The AI boom fills American RV parks
news.description: After the pandemic, the RV industry had weakened. The rise of data centers is reviving it by attracting workers to American RV parks.

news.title: Claude Fable 5.2 turns a prompt into a short film
news.description: Anthropic has launched Claude Fable 5.2, up to 30% faster than Fable 5.1 and available on paid Claude plans. Testers have used it to create videos and short animated films from a single prompt.

news.title: Instagram launches a free AI effects generator
news.description: Instagram’s Edits team has launched Effect Builder, a free web tool that turns a text description into an AI effect for Stories, without design or programming skills. The service is limited to the United States and people over 18.

news.title: Adobe and Disney partner to create custom AI models
news.description: Adobe and Disney have announced a multi-year partnership to create, through Firefly Foundry, generative models trained on Disney characters, environments, and visual styles. Walt Disney Imagineering is already using it for park design, including a model that transforms sketches into rendered 2D concepts.

news.title: Meta launches Muse Ember, a low-cost AI agent model
news.description: Meta has launched Muse Ember, its smallest model, which reportedly matches Claude Haiku 5.5 at about one-third of the per-task cost during agent steps run at scale.

news.title: Google unveils two new eighth-generation TPU chips
news.description: Google has introduced two new eighth-generation TPU chips, increasing pressure on Nvidia as competition for dedicated AI hardware intensifies.

news.title: Claude can audit your finances from CSV files
news.description: A creator demonstrates how to use Claude as a personal financial advisor by providing twelve months of bank transactions in CSV format. The process cleans the data, detects hidden subscriptions, and ranks expenses according to potential savings.

news.title: AARP publishes 12 tips for managing unwanted subscriptions
news.description: The guide covers monitoring price increases, setting calendar reminders, and what to do when a company refuses to cancel a subscription.

news.title: Apple explains how to cancel a subscription
news.description: The guide explains where to find each Apple charge so grouped line items can be linked to the relevant apps.

news.title: Google Play explains how to manage Android subscriptions
news.description: The help page explains how to cancel, pause, or change subscriptions billed through an Android phone.

news.title: The FTC directs users to ReportFraud to report recurring charges
news.description: The FTC’s ReportFraud website lets users report a charge that continues after a subscription has been canceled.

news.title: A free radio for listening to music in a Tesla
news.description: A Model Y owner recommends JSM Radio, which they use as their primary source of music in their car.

news.title: Can you accelerate while using autonomous driving?
news.description: A discussion considers whether it is possible to press the accelerator while Tesla’s autonomous driving is active.

news.title: Disable “Hey Grok” to avoid Grok surveillance
news.description: The discussion title recommends disabling the “Hey Grok” command to avoid being monitored by Grok.

news.title: A 12,318-mile cross-country trip in a Tesla
news.description: An owner recounts a 12,318-mile round trip across the country and the things that surprised them.

news.title: Discussion about energy consumption in Wh per mile
news.description: A discussion focuses on the energy consumption of Tesla vehicles, expressed in Wh per mile.

news.title: What is the best charging rate for a Tesla?
news.description: The title refers to a discussion about the best charging rate.

news.title: Should you leave the Tesla Wall Connector plugged in after 80%?
news.description: The discussion examines whether the Tesla Wall Connector should remain plugged in once the battery reaches 80%.

news.title: Scania goes from one person to 50 pilots through its customers
news.description: Scania’s Pilot Partner team launches a pilot only when a customer brings forward and funds a problem. This approach has helped deploy 400 electric buses in São Paulo and reshape the company’s strategy.

news.title: Supplier requests can reveal a deeper problem
news.description: An open innovation specialist was receiving mostly supplier requests from business units. During a discussion with five peers, she explored how to provide the requested supplier and then question the underlying need.

news.title: Six consumer-goods competitors share their pilots
news.description: AB InBev, Coca-Cola, Unilever, Danone, Colgate-Palmolive, and Mondelēz participate in the 100+ Accelerator. The program shares pilot results among its partners after one company defines the problem, funds the pilot, and evaluates its outcome.

news.title: How to choose the right AI model without exhausting your quota
news.description: Most labs offer three model tiers: a general-purpose model, a lighter version for simple tasks, and a more powerful version for ambitious projects. Anthropic’s guide recommends Opus 5.5 as a daily model, Sonnet 5.5 or Haiku 5.5 for simple tasks, and Fable 5.2 for complex projects.

news.title: An article examines why AI-generated texts are so frustrating
news.description: A new blog post examines in detail why readers dislike AI-generated texts and identifies three main flaws.

news.title: Anthropic shows a Fable-generated image that is hard to distinguish from a photograph
news.description: Anthropic asked its Fable model to create a painting presented as indistinguishable from a real photograph, then invited readers to determine whether the image was AI-generated.

news.title: Anthropic presents new experiments made with Fable
news.description: Anthropic published a new viral thread to showcase the capabilities of its latest Fable model.

news.title: A leadership lesson: helping your team overcome its fears
news.description: Bob Gilbreath recounts how an obstacle course organized with his team in 2015 strengthened the group’s confidence and led it to help a colleague overcome her fear. He encourages those who are hesitant to take the leap, also drawing on Joan Sotkin’s latest reflections on curiosity about oneself and change.

news.title: Microsoft opposes the U.S. ban on Chinese technology
news.description: Microsoft and industry groups oppose a proposed U.S. ban targeting Chinese optical transceivers used in data centers. They fear construction delays and unused AI chips due to a lack of sufficient alternative suppliers.

news.title: Panic over cloud capacity may be exaggerated
news.description: Claims that AWS and other cloud providers have sold all their AI capacity through 2027 overstate the shortages. Companies should distinguish between workload types, verify available capacity directly, and maintain flexible architectures.

news.title: IT leaders seek alternatives to SAP, VMware and Java
news.description: Rising license costs and support deadlines are prompting IT leaders to consider replacements for SAP, VMware and Oracle Java. However, integration, training and parallel-operation costs may exceed the license savings.

news.title: Cisco integrates Claude Mythos to test AI security
news.description: Cisco is integrating Anthropic’s Claude Mythos model into its AI Defense platform to improve adaptive security testing. The goal is to identify vulnerabilities and behavioral risks in AI agents within a controlled, authorized environment.

news.title: Google expands Gemini in Gmail to Workspace users
news.description: Google is extending email-thread summaries and the non-personalized “Help me write” feature to all Workspace users aged 18 and over. These features are enabled by default but can be disabled by users or administrators.

news.title: IBM expands Apptio tools to link AI spending with business value
news.description: IBM has expanded Apptio’s AI spending-tracking tools and Kubecost’s Kubernetes network cost reports. Features include AI usage connectors, financial planning, and greater visibility into certain AWS costs.

news.title: Docker Sandboxes isolate development environments
news.description: Docker Sandboxes provides isolated microVM-based development environments for building projects without cluttering the host system. Developers can create them with the sbx command, define network rules, and reproduce them using snapshots or declarative Dockerfiles.

news.title: Australian institution targets $2.1 million in savings with HPE
news.description: According to HPE, the Royal Australasian College of Surgeons cut its virtualization licensing bill by up to 70% and reduced its server fleet from eight to four. The organization expects total benefits of 2.1 million Australian dollars over five years.

news.title: CloudWatch Logs adds account-level retention policies
news.description: CloudWatch now supports retention policies that apply to an entire account or to log group prefixes.

news.title: Route 53 Profiles supports multiple profiles per VPC
news.description: Multiple Route 53 profiles can now be associated with the same VPC, allowing teams to manage separate DNS configurations with explicit priorities.

news.title: Purina turns smart feeder prototype into a connected product
news.description: Purina developed a cat feeder that identifies each animal and tracks its eating habits using vision, load sensors, and edge AI. With Edge Impulse, the team adapted its models to real-world household conditions.

news.title: Qualcomm launches RISC-V platform for connectivity and embedded AI
news.description: The Qualcomm QCC744-EVK platform, based on a RISC-V core, is now supported by Edge Impulse and Zephyr. It combines Wi-Fi 6, Bluetooth 5.4, IEEE 802.15.4, local sensors, and machine learning for smart connected devices.

news.title: Industrial laundry automates defect sorting with edge AI
news.description: A laundry company deployed an Edge AI solution in three months using Edge Impulse’s FOMO vision algorithm to distinguish shadows from stains on fast-moving sorting lines. The system freed about a dozen employees for higher-value tasks.

news.title: Industrial prototype detects failures and coordinates repairs itself
news.description: A conveyor system combines anomaly detection, agentic AI, a unified namespace, and a VENTUNO Q board to detect abnormal vibrations locally, analyze the problem, initiate maintenance, and reschedule production. The prototype runs at the edge without relying on the cloud.

news.title: Magnetic sensor enables AI to recognize movements without a camera
news.description: A project uses a Hall-effect sensor, a Seeed Studio Wio Terminal, and a magnetic toy car to recognize fast, slow, or nonexistent movements without images. The model achieves 100% accuracy on the controlled test set and performs inference in under one millisecond on the terminal.

news.title: Robot plays rock-paper-scissors and taunts its opponent
news.description: A robot plays rock-paper-scissors by combining gesture detection, a language model, and speech synthesis, all running locally on a Qualcomm Dragonwing IQ9 EVK platform. A webcam and a robotic hand complete the interactive setup.

news.title: Arduino VENTUNO Q combines CPU, GPU, and NPU for edge AI
news.description: The Arduino VENTUNO Q board is designed for demanding applications such as advanced robotics and physical AI by combining CPU, GPU, and NPU capabilities. Its native support in Edge Impulse enables algorithms to be developed, optimized, and deployed directly on the board.

news.title: XPeng plans to launch its flying car in China in summer 2027
news.description: XPeng’s two-seat flying car, priced at 300,000 dollars, is expected to be ready in the second half of 2027. It has six electric propellers, can fly 30 kilometers, and includes a six-wheeled van for transport.

news.title: Modern Web Guidance 1.0 brings web expertise to coding agents
news.description: Modern Web Guidance gives coding agents expertise in the web platform, best practices, and browser compatibility. Firefox and Edge are joining Chrome to improve cross-platform compatibility and contribute to the project.

news.title: “Glue work” remains harmful in the AI era
news.description: “Glue work” refers to processes that can be sustained only through engineers’ unrewarded sacrifice.

news.title: Sequoia Capital rethinks its investment model
news.description: Sequoia believes a more focused strategy will enable it to achieve better returns.

news.title: Reddit turns user conversations into AI-generated product reviews
news.description: Reddit Reviews is gradually rolling out to all users in the United States on iOS, Android, and the web.

news.title: Agent-traffic distinguishes AI agents from people and bots
news.description: Agent-traffic is a tool capable of distinguishing agents, AI crawlers, search-engine bots, and human users.

news.title: A winter storm could hit the U.S. East Coast this week
news.description: A nor’easter could bring cold temperatures to the East Coast later this week.

news.title: Société Générale anticipates a year-end stock market rally
news.description: The bank believes falling oil prices, post-election clarity and a trend reversal could support stocks through 2027. It is also proposing a strategy to benefit from the rally.

news.title: Nvidia would be worth 30% less without CEO Jensen Huang
news.description: According to analyst Dan Ives, Nvidia’s value depends heavily on Jensen Huang’s visibility and image, and he would be difficult to replace. Analysts nevertheless believe the controversy surrounding the executive should not affect TSMC’s business.

news.title: Investments in AI infrastructure could become obsolete
news.description: AI innovation is advancing so quickly that billions invested in infrastructure could become obsolete before generating a return on investment.

news.title: Handshake AI contractors say they were not paid in full
news.description: Joel Thomas says the startup owes him $11,000 in unpaid wages. Nearly two dozen current and former contractors told Business Insider that Handshake underpaid them.

news.title: Data center workers are living in RVs
news.description: Workers traveling across the United States for well-paying data center jobs sometimes choose to live in RVs. This is often cheaper than hotels and short-term rentals, and supports the RV industry.

news.title: Business Insider reveals its 20 real estate Rising Stars
news.description: Business Insider selected 20 young real estate professionals aged 35 or younger. They work in an industry being reshaped by AI, changes at listing sites and new tax rules.

news.title: Goldman Sachs, Cisco and JPMorgan restrict access to certain AI tools
news.description: After encouraging employees to adopt AI, several companies are taking a more targeted approach to deploying certain tools. The goal is to achieve better returns from these technologies rather than necessarily cut spending.

news.title: Venmo adds a receipt-scanning bill-splitting feature
news.description: The new feature lets users photograph a receipt, calculate each person’s taxes and tip, and then send Venmo payment requests. Business Insider tested it.

news.title: Students line up from 4:30 a.m. to land a job
news.description: Students get up very early and line up in an attempt to find a job.

news.title: John Turturro says he worked with abusive directors
news.description: John Turturro said he worked with directors he describes as abusive early in his career.

news.title: A family settled in Sweden struggles to preserve the life it built there
news.description: After moving to Sweden for the husband’s work four years ago, a family now says it is struggling to maintain the life it built there.

news.title: AI agents are almost absent from food and grocery orders
news.description: Almost no one uses AI agents to order food or groceries in apps such as Uber.

news.title: Boeing prepares 2,500 job cuts in its commercial airplanes business
news.description: Boeing sent a memo to staff as the company prepares to eliminate 2,500 jobs in its commercial airplanes business.

news.title: Pluto TV contracts as its free competitors gain share
news.description: Skydance-owned Pluto TV has shrunk as its free television competitors have gained market share.

news.title: A family that lived in an RV for 14 years remains attached to the lifestyle
news.description: After living in an RV for 14 years before joining Villa Vie Odyssey, the family says the ship’s halt has not changed how it wants to live.

news.title: Anthropic tests Claude Meetings to automate meetings
news.description: Claude Meetings joins a Google Meet call as a visible participant, drafts an agenda during the discussion, and then saves notes and action items. It does not join calls with external guests without an administrator’s approval.

news.title: Oura acquires Counsel Health for $625 million
news.description: Oura completed its acquisition of Counsel Health, an AI-powered primary care startup, for an announced $625 million.

news.title: Bay raises $50 million to secure enterprise agents
news.description: Bay emerged from stealth with $50 million to develop software that blocks risky actions by enterprise agents before they are executed.

news.title: Adobe introduces Creative Agent to automate creative edits
news.description: Adobe’s Creative Agent performs multi-step edits in Illustrator, Premiere, InDesign and After Effects from natural-language instructions. The tool is in beta.

news.title: STE80 Humanizer rewrites text that sounds AI-generated
news.description: STE80 Humanizer is a free, open-source tool that corrects markers of AI-generated text in two passes. The first removes 26 of them, while the second brings the text closer to simplified technical English.

news.title: Otter adds 13 transcription languages to all its plans
news.description: Otter added 13 transcription languages to all its plans, bringing the total to 17. Fourteen more languages and language switching during meetings are planned soon.

news.title: The U.S. and China create an alert channel for superintelligence
news.description: Washington and Beijing will share their methods for testing models and alert each other in the event of a serious incident. Neither country is committing to slow AI development, however.

news.title: Nvidia GR00T 2 learns robotic movements by watching humans
news.description: GR00T 2 transfers movements observed in human videos to robotic arms. The model was trained on about 400,000 hours of video, but its success rate varies depending on the task.

news.title: AI users work up to 90 minutes more per day
news.description: An ActivTrak analysis of 9,140 employees shows that AI users work 8.4 to 9.1 hours per day, compared with 7.6 hours for others. Heavy users also have focus periods that are 22% shorter.

news.title: Amazon releases Mitra-v2, an open-source model for completing tables
news.description: Mitra-v2 predicts missing values in a table from a few examples, without additional training. Trained on synthetic tables, it outperforms its predecessor on 32 of TabArena’s 33 datasets and is available under the Apache-2.0 license.

news.title: Booz Allen replaces Anthropic with Nvidia’s open-source models
news.description: The U.S. defense contractor has reportedly replaced Anthropic’s models with Nvidia’s Nemotron for its cybersecurity and defense software. Its developers continue to use Claude Code for programming.

news.title: Abliteration AI removes safeguards from open-weight models
news.description: Wired profiles Devon Thomas, an engineer who removes protections from powerful open-weight models and makes them accessible. He says he wants to enable legitimate uses, while critics point to the risks of unrestricted models.

news.title: eBay blocks AI agents that make purchases on users’ behalf
news.description: eBay is blocking Muse in particular, Meta’s agent that was preparing product selections for a reader of The Verge. The situation illustrates growing resistance from major platforms to agents that shop for users.

news.title: Adobe integrates with Gmail, Drive and Gemini as Google works on Photoshop
news.description: Adobe lets users open Acrobat directly from Google Drive and Gmail and is adding its connectors to Gemini and Google Search’s AI Mode. Google DeepMind and Adobe are also developing an image model for Photoshop capable of near-real-time edits.

news.title: Spotify’s AI DJ gets new voices and becomes less talkative
news.description: Premium subscribers can now choose from seven English voices and two Spanish voices for the AI DJ. An option limits its commentary to brief interludes at the beginning and end of listening.

news.title: A humanoid sorts parts at Mercedes-Benz with a 96% success rate
news.description: Google DeepMind and Apptronik are testing Gemini Robotics 2.5 on Mercedes-Benz production lines in Hungary and Germany. The Apollo 2 humanoid sorted metal parts there with a reported 96% success rate.

news.title: AI robots sort mixed waste with more than 95% accuracy
news.description: Nvidia is highlighting AIRECO, which recognizes plastics with more than 95% accuracy, and EverestLabs AI, which has deployed around 150 sorting robots. AIRECO’s future line is expected to increase capacity while sharply reducing operating costs.

news.title: Gemini for healthcare automates medical administrative tasks
news.description: Google Cloud links medical records, billing, clinical recommendations and Medicare data to automate tasks including record summarization and prior authorizations. The service is being tested in the United States under human supervision.

news.title: Lazarus shows that fewer than ten neurons can trap an AI agent
news.description: Microsoft Research shows that a backdoor can be hidden by reactivating fewer than ten dormant neurons, without retraining the model. An innocuous trigger can then prompt the agent to download and execute malicious code.

news.title: Ten WIRED experts detail the main dangers associated with AI
news.description: The experts interviewed mainly cite cyberattacks, biological attacks and the overly rapid adoption of unreliable systems in defense. They doubt that a pause could last in the face of economic pressure and consider governments too slow.

news.title: Investors flee tech amid AI-related spending
news.description: The Nasdaq fell 5.3% in October and the Kospi 16.2%, while capital shifted toward sectors considered more defensive. HSBC nevertheless believes Nvidia’s decline is excessive given its valuation multiples.
